title: Additional terms under § 2-207(2)
summary: An additional term addresses a matter added by an acceptance or confirmation to the offer or agreement. Section 2-207(2) determines whether such a proposed term becomes part of a contract.
notes:
Outside a transaction between merchants, additional terms are proposals requiring agreement. Between merchants, the subsection provides for their inclusion unless the offer limits acceptance, the addition materially alters the bargain, or timely objection occurs. Bayway examines the material-alteration exception for a tax-allocation clause. A term that conflicts with an existing term raises the separate different-terms problem in Northrop. The classification and formation route must therefore be identified before applying the exception.

The text identifies three exceptions: an offer expressly limiting acceptance, material alteration, and timely notification of objection. Bayway concerns the material-alteration exception and puts its proof on the opponent of inclusion. Nonmerchant transactions do not receive the same automatic incorporation rule, as Klocek emphasizes. Materiality must be assessed under the governing legal approach rather than reduced to the size of a payment.
